To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

online social networks are composed of three distinct components, each with its own characteristic structure, that these structures are the result of different mechanisms of growth, and that the structure of the network evolves over time as a result of changes in these mechanisms.

online social networks have a star-like structure, that the stars are not the core of the social networks, that there is a core of the social network that is not the core of its star structure, and that the social networks are growing in a way that is consistent with the model we have proposed.

(1) Online social networks are composed of three distinct components, a core giant component, an isolated component composed of stars, and an unconnected component of singletons; (2) The core giant component of an online social network is composed of two regions, a well-connected core region and a peripheral region of isolated users; and (3) A model of network growth that captures these features of component structure can be used to explain the observed evolution of these networks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of the network is determined by the interaction between inviters, who create isolated star-like structures, and linkers, who create a giant component.

the structure of these online networks is not a reflection of the underlying social structure of the people who participate in them.
